subject: AegisHealth RFP: Cutover sequencing & data-consistency protocols
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@aegishealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:32:00-08:00
Subject: RFP follow-up: detailed cutover sequencing and rollback expectations

Sofia,

Thanks for taking the time on the RFP. As part of our procurement review we need a detailed implementation plan that covers:
- Cutover sequencing for tenant onboarding and live traffic switch
- Data consistency checks and reconciliation steps (pre/post cutover)
- Canary gating criteria and rollback windows
- Dependencies on our KMS and logging (we run a managed Azure Key Vault instance)
- Expected maintenance windows and permitted outage windows for final go-live

Can you send a doc or runbook that lays this out with an estimated timeline, and confirm whether Redwood can meet a 4-hour rollback SLA if data divergence is detected? We have a procurement deadline of 2026-11-30.

Also loop in any technical leads who will own the cutover.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior IT Program Manager
AegisHealth
[procurement@aegishealth.com]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: detailed cutover sequencing and rollback expectations

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity and the deadline. We can produce an implementation runbook that covers the items you listed. High-level response first:
- Cutover sequencing: we propose a three-phase approach (staged pilot -> canary lane -> full cutover) with traffic split controls and health gating.
- Data consistency: automated pre-cutover checks, incremental sync verification, and a reconciliation job with checksum reporting.
- Canary gating: success criteria include 99.9% response parity on a sample prompt set, latency SLA met for 95th percentile, and no material quality regressions on customer prompts.
- Rollback SLA: we can commit to a 4-hour data-rollback window for transactional syncs if the deployment follows our recommended gating steps and we retain pre-cutover snapshots.

I asked Marissa (implementation lead) and Karthik (infra/runtime) to draft a runbook and an initial timeline. We aim to get a first-pass document to you by Monday 2026-11-15.

Would you prefer the runbook as a PDF + XLS timeline, or a collaborative Google Doc?

Best,
Sofia
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@aegishealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: [Draft] Cutover & canary runbook + timeline (v1.0)

Daniel / Sofia —

Attached is our draft runbook and an estimated timeline spreadsheet. Key highlights:
1) Pilot phase (2 weeks) — onboard 1 tenant into a dedicated canary pool; smoke tests and reconciliation run twice daily.
2) Canary phase (1 week) — split 5% traffic to canary lane; automated quality/regression checks run for 72 hours; manual sign-off required by Aegis ops.
3) Ramp (3 days) — progressively increase to 50% then 100% with traffic shaping rules; maintain KV cache warmers and KV cache preservation to reduce cold-start artifacts.
4) Cutover day — final snapshot, one-hour read-only window, apply config switch, run reconciliation, and monitor for 6 hours.

Rollback and data consistency notes:
- We maintain pre-cutover snapshots for up to 24 hours for immediate rollback.
- Reconciliation job compares checksums across the incremental sync window and reports anomalies; critical anomalies trigger automated rollback.
- For KMS: we support Azure Key Vault; see attached KMS-integration-diagram.png. We recommend a short test key rotation during pilot to confirm access patterns.

Acceptance gating in the runbook:
- Stability: 99.9% pass on health checks across canary requests for 72h
- Quality: no >5% increase in prompt mismatch rate vs baseline on a 500-sample prompt set
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms for the target model configuration

Attachments: AegisHealth_Migration_Timeline.xlsx, redwood-cutover-runbook-v1.3.pdf, KMS-integration-diagram.png

Questions for you: preferred maintenance window for final cutover (weekend overnight or weekday early morning)? Any constraints on snapshot retention beyond 24 hours?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <dpark@aegishealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [Draft] Cutover & canary runbook + timeline (v1.0)

On Tue, Nov 15, 2026 at 9:00 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Daniel / Sofia —
> 
> Attached is our draft runbook and an estimated timeline spreadsheet. Key highlights:
> 1) Pilot phase (2 weeks) — onboard 1 tenant into a dedicated canary pool; smoke tests and reconciliation run twice daily.

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from procurement and our security team:
- The 24-hour snapshot retention is shorter than our compliance window. We need a minimum of 7 days for final cutover snapshots. Can Redwood retain the final pre-cutover snapshot for 7 days?
- Regarding the KMS integration: can you confirm whether private key operations happen within our tenant boundary (no key material exported to Redwood)? We need a statement for the security questionnaire.
- Rollback SLA: your email mentions automated rollback for critical anomalies — can you specify the escalation steps and who will execute the rollback (Aegis ops vs Redwood engineers)? We need a runbook excerpt to attach to the procurement packet.

Finally, our preferred cutover window is Saturday 02:00–06:00 ET. Please confirm if that conflicts with your support coverage.

-Daniel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@aegishealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [Draft] Cutover & canary runbook + timeline (v1.0)

Daniel —

Short answers to your security/procurement items:
- Snapshot retention: we can extend the final pre-cutover snapshot retention to 7 days for this engagement. We'll flag it as an exception in the SLA addendum (attached summary: ea-sla-exception-summary.docx).
- KMS: private key operations remain in your tenant boundary when you provision keys in your Azure Key Vault and grant Redwood the 'unwrapKey' permission for the service principal. No key material is exported to Redwood. I attached a diagram and the minimal permission set.
- Rollback execution: automated rollback is triggered by the reconciliation engine when checksum divergence exceeds the configured threshold. Tiering:
  * Automated rollback attempt (0–30m): initiated by Redwood automation
  * Manual rollback (if automation fails or for data-edge cases): executed by Redwood infra lead with Aegis ops watching and with a runbook command list; typical manual window target is 180–240 minutes from anomaly detection.

We will include the exact runbook excerpt for procurement. The Saturday 02:00–06:00 ET window is compatible with our on-call rotation; we will schedule a dedicated on-call engineer and a program lead for the cutover window.

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ea-sla-exception-summary.docx]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@aegishealth.com>, AegisHealth Procurement <procurement@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [Draft] Cutover & canary runbook + timeline (v1.0)

Daniel —

Thanks for the questions and for the preferred window. Attached is the consolidated runbook (redwood-cutover-runbook-v1.3.pdf) with the procurement-ready excerpt inserted on pg. 8 ("Rollback execution and responsibilities"). Highlights:
- Snapshot retention extended to 7 days for the pre-cutover snapshot (SLA addendum attached).
- KMS: we require a service principal with unwrapKey; no key material leaves your Azure tenant. Security statement is included in the runbook appendix.
- Rollback SLA: automated rollback attempt within 30 minutes of detection; estimated manual rollback completion within 4 hours from detection for the scenarios defined as "critical anomalies." The runbook lists escalation contacts and a one-click rollback command sequence for infra.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the Saturday 02:00–06:00 ET window and provide the list of Aegis on-call contacts.
2) We will prepare the procurement packet (runbook excerpt + security statement + SLA addendum) and send DocuSign links for the exception addendum by COB 2026-11-24.

I've included the DocuSign link here for signature when you're ready: https://app.docusign.com/AEG-2026-578/sign

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
